items.title: $95,000 Grant Will Train Youth Ambassadors to Fight Islamophobia in Brampton and Mississauga
items.summary: According to INsauga, a new Safe Voices Peel initiative aimed at combating Islamophobia in Brampton and Mississauga has received more than $95,000 in funding from the province of Ontario. The outlet reports Zee Hamid, the MPP for Milton, announced Wednesday that $95,100 would go to Building Multicultural Communities through the province's Safer and Vital Communities Grant. INsauga reports the money will support a program that trains youth ambassadors in hate crime prevention, community safety and bystander intervention, with the initiative running in both cities. According to the outlet, organizers are partnering with Peel Regional Police, Brampton Library, Our Place Peel and other local community groups to deliver the program. Hamid said building safer communities starts at the grassroots level, according to INsauga. The outlet reports the initiative is expected to bring youth and community organizations together to raise awareness about hate prevention and encourage residents to take an active role in creating safer, more inclusive neighbourhoods.

items.title: TK Ultra Lounge Among Four Mississauga Businesses Handed Conditional Health Passes
items.summary: According to Mississauga.com, Peel Public Health issued conditional passes to three Mississauga restaurants and a medical esthetics spa following recent inspections. The outlet reports Peel Public Health inspectors routinely check restaurants, cocktail bars, beverage rooms, bakeries, takeout establishments and other businesses to ensure they meet food and personal service safety standards. Mississauga.com reports TK Ultra Lounge, a restaurant at 1 Derry Road, was among the businesses inspected, with its inspection taking place on August 25. According to the outlet, a green pass indicates a business is meeting requirements under Ontario's Health Protection and Promotion Act, while a conditional pass signals violations inspectors found during a visit. Mississauga.com notes the routine inspection program gives residents a way to check the food and personal-service safety record of local businesses.

items.title: Child E-Scooter Injuries Jump 29 Per Cent at Mississauga Hospitals This Spring
items.summary: According to Mississauga.com, two Mississauga hospitals recorded a 29 per cent jump in e-scooter-related emergency room visits this spring compared with the same period last year, with children under 18 making up a growing share of the cases. The outlet reports Credit Valley Hospital and Mississauga Hospital logged 134 emergency department visits tied to e-scooter injuries between April and June, according to data Trillium Health Partners provided to the publication, up 30 visits from the same three months in 2025. Mississauga.com reports children under 18 accounted for 65 per cent of those visits, compared with 49 per cent during the same stretch a year earlier. The outlet notes e-scooters are legal in Mississauga, but enforcement of e-scooter and e-bike violations falls to Peel Regional Police rather than the city. According to Mississauga.com, the Canadian Paediatric Surveillance Program's newly published 2025 results identified 57 severe e-scooter and e-bike injury cases among children and youth nationwide. The outlet frames the local numbers as part of a broader pattern of underage riding and enforcement gaps playing out across the city.

items.title: Sudbury Drug Raid Nets Mississauga Man, Loaded Handgun and $50,000 in Cocaine
items.summary: According to the Greater Sudbury Police Service, detectives with the force's Drug Enforcement Unit arrested a Mississauga man as he entered Greater Sudbury on August 23, concluding a drug trafficking investigation. Police say the arrest, carried out with help from the Emergency Response Unit and Community Response Unit, was followed by a search of the man incident to arrest that turned up roughly 500 grams of cocaine, a loaded Ruger semi-automatic handgun, four cell phones and $3,000 in Canadian currency. According to police, investigators then executed a Controlled Drugs and Substances Act search warrant at a downtown Greater Sudbury residence connected to the accused. The search of that residence turned up an additional $500 in cash along with digital scales, packaging materials and cutting agents, police say. The Greater Sudbury Police Service reports the estimated street value of the seized cocaine is approximately $50,000.

items.title: Nearly 500 Newcomers Have Taken Mississauga's Free Water Safety Course Since 2024
items.summary: According to INsauga, the City of Mississauga says nearly 500 people who have moved to Canada within the past five years have enrolled in its free Swim to Survive program for newcomers since the initiative launched in summer 2024. INsauga reports the program, delivered through the Lifesaving Society, is aimed at preventing drowning and water-related injuries by teaching what city officials call the essential skills every Canadian should know in a water emergency. According to the outlet, the free program is open to newcomers ages eight and older and consists of three one-hour classes covering how to roll into deep water, tread water for one minute and swim 50 metres. City officials told INsauga the program addresses a critical but often overlooked aspect of settlement in water safety as Mississauga continues to welcome new residents. INsauga notes the program's popularity reflects a broader push by the city to make water safety education accessible to newcomer families.

items.title: Windsor Arrest Near U.S. Border Leads to Murder Charges in 2022 Toronto Studio Shooting
items.summary: According to INsauga, Toronto police say a Mississauga man has been charged with two counts of second-degree murder and one count of attempted murder in connection with a 2022 shooting inside a music studio in west Toronto. INsauga reports the suspect, 25-year-old Darriel Thompson, was arrested by Windsor police on August 22 near the U.S. border and was scheduled to appear in a Toronto court the day the charges were announced. The outlet reports the shooting killed Minyali Wur, 24, and Chudier Reat, 20, both of Mississauga, on January 3, 2022, at a studio on Thirtieth Street just east of the Mississauga border. According to INsauga, police also found an injured woman at the scene that night, and all three victims were taken to hospital, where the two Mississauga men later died of their injuries while the woman survived. INsauga notes the studio's address also housed offices and apartments in the same building.

items.title: Ward 7 Draws 17 Council Candidates as Mississauga's Municipal Race Takes Shape
items.summary: According to INsauga, 75 candidates, including nine incumbents, are running for city council seats across Mississauga's 11 wards in the October 26 municipal election, a race that has drawn less attention than the crowded 14-candidate mayoral contest. INsauga reports that because sitting councillors Alvin Tedjo of Ward 2 and Dipika Damerla of Ward 7 both entered the mayoral race, at least two new faces are guaranteed to join council for its next term. The outlet notes those same two wards feature the largest candidate fields, with 17 people vying for the Ward 7 seat anchored by Cooksville and 14 hopefuls competing in Ward 2, which covers Clarkson and Lorne Park in the city's southwest. According to INsauga, Ward 5, which includes the Malton area and is historically among the most closely contested in the city, has 10 candidates running, including incumbent Natalie Hart. INsauga reports candidate nominations closed this past Friday, meaning both the mayoral and council races are now officially set.
